text:
The strangest thing about Nikita Kucherov's trade request is how little it has shown up on the ice. He asked out of Tampa Bay at the end of October, the league has spent a week drawing up landing spots (Sportsnet ran a list, The Athletic reranked the power rankings around his impact), and last night in Minnesota he scored the overtime winner after the Lightning came back from two goals down. Tampa has won three straight with 61% of the expected goals in those games (expected goals measure the quality of chances). Whatever the room feels like, the hockey has been good.

The other goaltending story in Tampa is the reassuring one: Andrei Vasilevskiy's agent has indicated he intends to finish his career with the Lightning. His season has not caught up with that commitment yet. He is at .886 and -0.5 goals saved above expected after a +23.2 season, and he is the projected starter on the second night of a back-to-back.

Winnipeg is in a different place. The Jets are 2-3-0 in their last five and our numbers give them a 14% shot at the playoffs, but this week had life in it: a historic comeback in Montreal sparked by Tyrel Bauer's Gordie Howe hat trick, then a 6-2 rout of Vancouver. Stuart Skinner signed a two-year deal on Thursday and has won two straight. Josh Morrissey (wrist) has been out, and Ken Wiebe of the Winnipeg Free Press raised the possibility of a return on Sunday; until he's back, Neal Pionk runs the first power play.

The matchup still tilts hard. Tampa has taken 55% of the five-on-five expected goals, Winnipeg 47%, and the Lightning won the first meeting 6-4 on Oct 29, a game they deserved 76% of the time. Kyle Connor (43% to score) is the Jet most likely to change that. Our sleeper is Tampa's Pontus Holmberg, a third-liner with 2.5 expected goals in his last ten. Our numbers make it 3.47 expected goals to 2.89 for the Lightning.
headline: Kucherov wants out, and keeps winning games anyway

hunch.text: Our numbers like Tampa Bay by a lot. Our gut says the second night of a back-to-back, a Vasilevskiy who hasn't found his game yet and a Jets team that has looked alive this week add up to a Winnipeg win.
